findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the served-streak lifecycle unambiguously: where it increments (which call outcome), where it resets (relative to record_executed), and how the guard's entry-time arm-2 check orders against the memo's later record_executed for the SAME call under the guard-outermost composition.
evidence: Guard stays OUTERMOST (Guard->Memo->Steering), so the guard's call_tool runs and checks the streak BEFORE delegating down to the memo layer that will (or will not) call record_executed for that same call — plan does not state how the entry-time check reconciles with the later executed-record for the SAME call

Plan specifies the CHECK point ('before increment') and that 'policy responses never reset the streak', but never states the INCREMENT site (which calls increment the served-streak) nor the RESET site relative to record_executed
findings.finding: The served-streak counter's increment and reset placement is ambiguous given the pinned guard-outermost order: the guard checks the streak 'at call entry, before increment', but at call entry the memo layer has not yet decided whether THIS call is served or executed, so the plan does not specify when the streak is incremented for a served call, when record_executed resets it, and how the two order within a single call's lifetime.
findings.location: Approach: 'a served-streak backstop ... after a FULL window of consecutive zero-execution calls (checked at call entry, before increment)'; 'the memo layer calls record_executed at each site that performs real work'
scenarios: An executed call: guard checks streak at entry (streak still high from prior served calls), then memo records executed further down — if the check fires before the reset, an executed call could trip arm 2 one call too early
Off-by-one at the window boundary: whether the Nth zero-execution call trips depends on whether increment happens before or after the entry-time check
